intro.title: What is easyrender?
intro.body: easyrender is an image-to-3D tool: it turns one photo of a piece of furniture, a decor object or a building exterior into a 3D model. First it draws the object from every side, a free angle sheet you can check before you spend anything. If the preview looks right, one click turns it into a 3D model you can spin and download as GLB and USDZ.
intro.scope: It does not model whole rooms. It does not invent measurements. You get the file; you decide if it is good enough to keep.
intro.secondaryCta: See models made from a photo

pricing.title: Pay per model. Credits never expire.
pricing.description: Previews are free. A finished 3D model costs {credits} credits ({price}).

features.ar: Coming soon: see it in your room from your phone

connect.a: easyrender is an MCP server. Add it to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client with your API key, and your agent can turn photos into 3D models on its own. Everything it makes shows up in your web dashboard.

needAgent.q: Do I need an agent to use it?
needAgent.a: No. You can upload photos in the web app, one by one or in bulk from your library. The agent just lets you run it on autopilot.

photos.a: One sharp, well lit photo where the whole object is visible, ideally on a plain background. Catalogue shots and listing photos of a single piece, or a clear photo of a building front, work well. Busy backgrounds, cropped objects, heavy blur or very fine detail give a weaker preview.

scope.a: Furniture, decor objects and building exteriors, from a single photo. It models one object at a time, not whole interior rooms. Fine logos and small text often come out soft.

output.a: A free preview that shows the object from every angle, then — if you spend credits — a 3D model you can spin on its page and download as a textured GLB for the web and a USDZ file.

freePreview.a: Before the 3D model is built we draw the object from every angle. You check that preview at no cost and only spend credits when the shape and the details look right.

failed.a: If the 3D model fails to build, the credits for that render go back to your balance automatically.

public.a: Finished models appear in the public gallery by default. You can switch off “Show in public gallery” on the model’s page. Today, hiding a model may also stop its link from opening for other people, so keep it in the gallery if you want to share the link.

cost.q: How much does a 3D model cost?
cost.a: Previews are free. A finished 3D model costs {credits} credits, and credits cost {unit} each, so a model is {price}. Credits never expire. The pricing page lists every pack.

what.a: easyrender is a web app that turns one photo of an object into a 3D model. You upload the photo, check a free sheet that shows the object from every angle, and spend credits only if you want the finished model, which you download as GLB and USDZ.

formats.q: Which file formats can I download?
formats.a: Two: a textured GLB, for the web and most 3D tools, and a USDZ, for Apple devices. The model keeps its shape and materials, not real-world measurements or scale.

ar.q: Can I see the model in my room?
ar.a: Augmented reality is coming soon: you will be able to open the model on your phone and place it in your room. It shows the shape and materials of the object, not its real-world size.

Models.metaTitle: Models: what easyrender runs on · easyrender
Models.metaDescription: The two models behind every easyrender render, the settings they run with and what each step costs in credits. A failed step is refunded.
Models.title: The models behind every render
Models.description: Two models, one after the other: the first draws your photo from every side, the second builds the 3D file from those drawings. Here is which, with what settings, and what each step costs.

sheet.title: Angle sheet
sheet.role: Draws the object from eight sides plus a top view on one 2K sheet, from your photo and a short prompt. You see it before any 3D is built.

settings.prompt: Prompt: a fixed turnaround brief, plus guidance for the product category and its material

build.title: 3D build
build.role: Rebuilds a textured 3D model from your photo and the eight sheet views. The result downloads as GLB and USDZ.

pricing.title: What each step costs
pricing.note: The sheet is free as a daily preview. A credit costs {unit} and never expires. If a step fails, its credits are refunded.

change.title: What can change
change.body: Prompts and model settings can be tuned without a release. The models and their prices are fixed in the app, so the credits on the button are what you pay.

Evals.metaTitle: Evals: how renders are checked · easyrender
Evals.metaDescription: How easyrender scores its own renders: the five criteria, the checks that run on every render, and the results of each published run.
Evals.title: How we check renders
Evals.description: Every render passes automatic checks before it is stored. Separately, a run renders a golden set of product photos and scores them against five criteria, so a change to a prompt or a model shows up as a number.

checks.title: Checked on every render
checks.description: These checks already run in production. A render that fails one is not delivered, and its credits are refunded.
checks.photo: Photo: at least {min} px on the short side, under {max} px on the long side, no wider than {aspect}:1 and not a flat colour. It is rejected before any model runs, so it costs nothing.
checks.sheet: Sheet: at least {side} px, the object visible in at least {cells} of the 9 cells, and no more than {repeats} of the 8 turnaround views repeated.
checks.file: 3D file: a complete GLB (binary glTF, version 2) of more than {kb} KB.

criteria.title: What a run scores
criteria.description: Each photo of the golden set is rendered with the live pipeline and scored on five criteria, pass or fail.

shape.title: Shape and proportions
shape.description: The model keeps the shape, proportions and parts of the photographed object, with nothing added or removed.

views.title: Eight different views
views.description: The eight turnaround views of the sheet are different pictures, and the object is in every cell.

material.title: Material realism
material.description: The object looks makeable in its material: stone cut or carved and never bent, wood with the grain along each part, metal tube bending in smooth arcs.

finish.title: Colour and finish
finish.description: Colour, texture and finish (polished, brushed, matte) match the photo.

file.title: A valid file
file.description: The GLB opens, is complete and passes the file check.

results.title: Results
results.emptyBody: The first run is published here. Until then this page shows no scores, and none are made up.
